definitions.explanation: A person who learns from a master, especially in traditional arts, martial arts, crafts, or religious contexts. Implies a close mentorship relationship.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{画家|がか}の{弟子|でし}だ。
examples.english: He is a disciple of a famous painter.

examples.japanese: {師匠|ししょう}と{弟子|でし}の{関係|かんけい}は{特別|とくべつ}だ。
examples.english: The relationship between master and disciple is special.

examples.japanese: {弟子|でし}{入|い}りを{志願|しがん}した。
examples.english: I applied to become an apprentice.

notes:
USAGE: More formal than {生徒|せいと} (student) and implies a traditional master-apprentice relationship.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{弟子|でし}{入|い}りする (to become an apprentice)
・{内|うち}{弟子|でし} (live-in apprentice)
・{高|たか}{弟|でい} (top disciple, senior student)

CONTRAST:
・{師匠|ししょう} (master) - the teacher in this relationship
・{生徒|せいと} - student (more general, school context)
・{門下生|もんかせい} - student of a school/tradition
